comments.body:
PROVEN RCA / CLASSIFICATION (rebar-debug Phase 1, refreshed against origin/main 89128b2e09)

Mechanism: linked worktrees have distinct per-worktree git dirs but share one git common dir. Git stores the newest stash at the shared ref `refs/stash`; bare `git stash pop` selects `stash@{0}`, the newest entry in that repository-wide reflog, without recording or checking the creating worktree. Therefore two interleaved push/pop sequences can silently apply each other's changes. This is Git's documented design, not a Git defect.

Discriminating runtime proof: in isolated `/tmp/rebar-prudent-stash.c7Ipdk`, worktrees A and B reported different `--git-dir` paths but the same `--git-common-dir`. A stashed deletion A, then B stashed deletion B, producing `stash@{0}: B-owned-by-wt-b` and `stash@{1}: A-owned-by-wt-a`. Bare `git stash pop` in A applied B's deletion; bare pop in B then applied A's deletion. Final observable state was `wt-a: D b-owned.txt` and `wt-b: D a-owned.txt`. This confirms shared-ref/top-of-stack selection and rejects both a worktree-local stash-stack hypothesis and a wrong-worktree-path hypothesis. No shared repository stash was mutated.

Defect legitimacy is intentionally split because the ticket combines different decisions:

1. DEFECT / incomplete safety documentation: `AGENTS.md:100-131` explicitly promotes parallel-agent work; `AGENTS.md:217-220` mandates fresh linked worktrees; `Makefile:157-179` makes that workflow one command. The original agent-fitness change `c5d79b58b6` explicitly hardened concurrency and introduced this parallel workflow, and `minor-haste-ogle` establishes non-destructive preservation of work as a safety invariant. Yet the only stash warning is `AGENTS.md:264-267`, narrowly scoped to the shared main checkout; no adjacent guidance explains that stash is repository-global across every linked worktree. That omission permits behavior contrary to the approved safe-parallel-work intent. An adjacent warning plus worktree-local alternatives is a legitimate Phase-2 repair. Closed `sultanlike-doughty-civet` is direct prior art: `AGENTS.md:234-240` already teaches the analogous shared-common-dir hook hazard.

2. INTENDED UPSTREAM BEHAVIOR: the global `refs/stash` stack itself is working as Git defines it. Rebar cannot treat it as a worktree-local facility.

3. DESIGN DECISION / feature request: a mechanical repository-wide `git stash` blocker is not a straightforward hook fix. An isolated probe showed `git config alias.stash ...` cannot shadow Git's built-in `stash`; Git exposes no pre-stash or general pre-command hook. A PATH-level `git` wrapper would be bypassable and would intercept every Git consumer, including rebar internals, so adopting it changes repository tooling architecture and needs an explicit decision rather than automatic bug repair.

4. OPERATIONAL COORDINATION: returning the displaced ADR 0061 work and later deleting its stash/backup is not a code repair. It was deliberately left untouched; cleanup requires confirmation from that work's owner.

Sibling sweep: `src/rebar/_store/push.py:203-260` still issues `git stash push`, then bare `git stash pop`; `_resolve_conflicted_pop` also drops the current top entry at `push.py:197-200`. The ticket-store write lock does not serialize this repository-global stack against an agent in another linked worktree. Closed `filmy-basin-chasm` repaired pop-conflict cleanup but retained the assumption that the top stash belongs to rebar. This is a distinct executable sibling hazard and should receive its own Phase-1 proof/design disposition before changing the approved Tier-D stash/merge behavior (`docs/bash-migration.md:261-365`).

Shared-common-dir sweep disposition: hooks are already fixed/documented by `sultanlike-doughty-civet`; refs, object storage, and repository config are also shared by design but are not inherently destructive stack operations. The live high-risk stack-like construct found is stash, including the internal `push.py` caller above.

Recommended disposition: proceed automatically only with the adjacent documentation/safe-alternatives defect. Ask the operator to decide separately whether to adopt a Git wrapper or another enforcement architecture, and how to replace/serialize rebar's internal stash dance. Preserve the displaced stash and backup until their owner confirms recovery. No code edit, claim, transition, stash mutation, or cleanup was performed in Phase 1.

comments.body: Reassessed against current origin/main 51da20e753 (2026-08-10): partially resolved, not complete. ab0e7f577f removed rebar's own use of the repository-wide stash stack; ade954fcd3 repaired stranded-index handling; 19341e2edb improved foreign-path reporting; and 51da20e753 added the supported tracker-maintenance path and bans stash inside the tracker. The broader agent hazard remains: canonical worktree guidance still does not plainly warn that source-worktree stashes share one repository-wide stack, and there is no general mechanical guard preventing agents from using it. Keep this ticket open for that remaining scope.

compiled_state.description:
## The hazard, and it already caused a live incident

`git stash` writes to the SHARED git common dir, not to the worktree. On this host there are
roughly 30 worktrees with multiple agents working concurrently, so the stash is a single global
stack that every agent pushes to and pops from.

Two agents stashing at overlapping times will pop EACH OTHER'S uncommitted work into the wrong
worktree.

## Confirmed incident 2026-08-05

An agent working bug c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af used `git stash` twice to check whether a test failure
was pre-existing. On the second use a concurrent agent's stash operation interleaved, and it
popped the OTHER agent's changes into its worktree while its own went to theirs.

It recovered only because it happened to hold out-of-band copies. The displaced work was
preserved two ways and is STILL SITTING THERE at time of filing:

    stash@{0}: On fix-c5b3-scc-byfile: RECOVERED measurement-provenance work
               (ADR 0061 / det_measurement_provenance) displaced into worktree
               fix-c5b3-scc-byfile by a shared-stash race;
               backup at /tmp/RECOVERED-stash-race

ACTION NEEDED INDEPENDENT OF THIS BUG: that is another session's work on ADR 0061 /
det_measurement_provenance. Whoever owns it likely does not know it was displaced. It should be
returned to its owner before anything prunes the stash or clears /tmp.

## Why this is a rebar problem and not just a git fact

rebar's own guidance actively produces the conditions for it. AGENTS.md mandates working in
fresh worktrees, and `make worktree` makes spinning them up a single command. The
parallel-agent workflow is a documented, encouraged pattern. So the project tells agents to run
many worktrees in parallel while `git stash` — a reflex command for "let me check this against
a clean tree" — is silently global across all of them.

The failure is also SILENT and DESTRUCTIVE: `git stash pop` succeeds, the wrong files appear,
and nothing indicates the content came from another worktree. An agent that then commits has
committed someone else's work; an agent whose changes vanished may conclude its edits were
never made.

## What agents should do instead (all worktree-local)

- A throwaway worktree for the clean-tree comparison:
  `git worktree add /tmp/<unique> origin/main --detach`
- `git archive <ref>` to materialize a specific tree shape (ticket 7e90's agent did exactly
  this successfully to reproduce a pre-gate `.github/` layout).
- `git diff > /tmp/<unique>.patch` + `git checkout -- <paths>`, re-applied with `git apply`.
- Plain file copies inside the agent's own worktree directory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AGENTS.md states plainly that `git stash` is UNSAFE in this repo's parallel-worktree
      workflow, with the worktree-local alternatives above, sited where an agent reaching for
      stash will actually see it (near the worktree/parallel-agent guidance, not an appendix).
- [ ] The reason is given, not just the prohibition — an agent that understands the stash is
      global will generalize; one told a bare rule will work around it.
- [ ] Consider a mechanical block rather than relying on agents reading docs: evaluate whether
      a pre-commit or wrapper can refuse `git stash` when more than one worktree exists, and
      either implement it or record why not.
- [ ] The displaced ADR 0061 work above is returned to its owner or confirmed no longer needed,
      and the stash entry and /tmp backup are cleaned up only after that.
- [ ] Sweep for other git commands with the same shared-common-dir property and document any
      found (hooks are already known-shared — bug 84aa records a worktree-wide hook clobber
      from the same root cause, which suggests this class is recurring).

## Provenance

Reported by the agent that hit it while working c5b3. Bug 84aa is prior art for the same class:
hooks live in the shared common dir, so installing one from a linked worktree clobbered it for
every worktree at once.
compiled_state.title: git stash is SHARED across all worktrees, so parallel agents silently swap each other's uncommitted work
